clue.text: Good beer — quite a draught!

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker praises a fine pint and the hearty swig they take of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draught' looks like a drink of beer, but here it means a current of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale is a very strong wind, so it is a draught on a grand scale.

clue.text: Group of ten became rotten, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the clue words are to be said out loud and the spelling taken from what is heard

parts.note: to become rotten is to decay, past tense decayed

explanation.surface: A set of ten things went bad, so the rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade is a set of ten, most often ten years but also ten beads of a rosary.

clue.text: Moody learner into something sticky

indicators.note: the learner's letter goes into the sticky stuff, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: gum is a sticky substance
L is for learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A sulky novice has got stuck in something gluey.
explanation.definitionFit: Glum describes a gloomy, sullen mood.

clue.text: Junior public school type obtained something to eat

parts.note: at British public (private boarding) schools a fag was a junior boy who ran errands for a senior
got means obtained

explanation.surface: A young boarding-school pupil gets hold of a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A FAGGOT in Britain is a meatball of offal and herbs, traditionally served with gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: A faggot is a traditional British meatball made from offal, a dish for a meal.

clue.text: Recall important lady upsetting someone in club

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the lady's letters upside down, so they are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen, the most important lady
a member is someone who belongs to a club

explanation.surface: Bringing to mind a grand woman who annoyed a fellow at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' looks like annoyance in the surface; in this down clue it turns ER upwards to make RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind, a synonym.

clue.text: Take counsel, being cautious

explanation.surface: Advice on how to weigh matters with care.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to weigh matters up and discuss them; as an adjective, careful and unhurried in action.

clue.text: Like mother hen type with the potential to make male rant

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rearranged into something new, so they are to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A fussy, protective sort who could provoke a man into ranting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother hen is fussily protective, behaving in a motherly way.

clue.text: Observes section being rebuilt

indicators.note: the letters of the word section are put together again in another order

explanation.surface: An inspector watches part of a building under reconstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or spot, so the third-person forms match.

clue.text: Everyone has crammed the night before exam

indicators.note: the word for everyone has the other piece stuffed inside it

parts.note: all means everyone
eve is the evening or day before an event

explanation.surface: All the students revised hard the evening before their test.
explanation.walkthrough: An A LEVEL is the British school-leaving exam taken around age eighteen; 'crammed' suggests revision but marks the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A level is a British advanced school examination, one kind of test.

clue.text: Gasp about limited education? He might well!

definitions.text: Gasp about limited education? He might well!

indicators.note: the word for gasp goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
ED is a shortened form of education

explanation.surface: Someone tuts in horror at a poor schooling, as a stickler would.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a fussy stickler is just the person to gasp at poor education.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is a stickler for correctness, who would be appalled by sloppy learning.

clue.text: Attractive snare that's marvellous on the outside

indicators.note: the word for marvellous sits around the other piece, wrapping it

parts.note: magic is informal for marvellous
a net is a snare for catching animals

explanation.surface: A wonderful trap with a lovely exterior lures its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic means having the power to draw others in, like a magnet's pull.

clue.text: Policeman can be soft, surprisingly, in s. American country

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the country's name

parts.note: Chile is a country in South America

indicators.note: signals the three words are rearranged in an unexpected way

explanation.surface: A tough cop in South America turns out unexpectedly gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft' and 'surprisingly' suggest a gentle cop, but 'surprisingly' shuffles the three words and 'in' sets them inside the country. A chief constable heads a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief constable is the senior officer in charge of a British police force.

clue.text: Confrontation when two nuts meet

explanation.surface: A showdown pictured as two heads colliding.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct face-off between rivals; and nut is slang for the skull, so two of them meeting are a pair of heads touching.

clue.text: Knight getting help, bringing in a nymph

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: the word for help takes the extra letter inside it

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A knight finds assistance, which includes a water spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Damage limb, needing to go to hospital

indicators.note: the limb has to go to the hospital, so its letters follow the hospital's letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: An injured arm has to be taken to the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is injury or damage, a synonym.

clue.text: Behave amorously? Vole could!

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer is an instruction: make (rearrange) the second word, and the little rodent's letters result

explanation.surface: Could a vole really be romantic? Apparently so.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as cryptic wordplay: its first word is an anagram signal and its second word rearranged gives VOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make love is to have sex, the fullest way of being romantic with someone.

clue.text: Quiet yet?

explanation.surface: A question about whether things have calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and silent; and an adverb meaning even now or up to this time.

clue.text: Depressed by learning

explanation.surface: Feeling down after a study session.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low down is being miserable; and the lowdown is inside information, the facts one learns.

clue.text: Stray duck eaten by farm animal

indicators.note: the duck ends up inside the animal, swallowed whole

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep on a farm
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence O

explanation.surface: A wandering duck is gobbled up by a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander or stray without a fixed course.

clue.text: Humiliating part of job after the washing's dried?

definitions.text: part of job after the washing's dried?

explanation.surface: A household chore of taking in the laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone down a peg is humbling them; and literally, removing a clothes peg is part of fetching dry washing off the line.

clue.text: Simpleton's food

explanation.surface: A fool's meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for a silly person; and a strip of pasta eaten in soups and stir-fries.

clue.text: Star one found engraved into church table

indicators.note: the digit is cut into the table, so it sits inside the word

parts.note: an altar is the table in a church where communion is prepared
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single figure is carved into the communion table.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Youngster, almost complete hooligan, getting to relax

indicators.note: the word for youngster stops short of its final letter

parts.note: a child is a youngster
a lout is a thorough yob or hooligan

explanation.surface: A young lout is learning to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill out is slang for unwinding, an idiom meaning relax.

clue.text: Sharp projection gets bottom of boat on river

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of the word is its final letter

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A boat's hull catches on something sharp in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusk is a long pointed tooth that sticks out, as on an elephant.

clue.text: What one goes through between successive dos?

definitions.text: What one goes through between successive dos?

parts.words: What one goes through between successive dos?
parts.note: dos look like parties, but they are the note do in the sol-fa scale; singing up from one do to the next covers eight notes

explanation.surface: What a party-goer endures from one celebration to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dos' reads as parties, but it is the plural of do, the first note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is the eight-note interval spanning one do to the next in the scale.

clue.text: Opening hospital department after five

indicators.note: in this down clue the department comes after the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A hospital ward opens after five o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an opening that lets air or gas escape.

clue.text: Butter about to be added to meat — not a surprising thing

indicators.note: the word for butter is turned around, read back to front

parts.note: a ram is a butter, an animal that butts with its head

indicators.note: the meat loses the letter named next to it

parts.note: veal is the meat of a calf

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: add butter to the meat, nothing remarkable about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread but is something that butts: RAM, turned by 'about' to MAR. VEAL with 'not a' becomes VEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is a wonder, something that astonishes.

clue.text: Feeling terribly intense over time

indicators.note: signals the letters of intense are mixed up badly

explanation.surface: Emotions running very high for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' looks like an intensifier for 'intense' but shuffles that word; 'over' is a link putting the time letter after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means capable of feeling or perceiving, an adjective matching feeling.
